"It's going to be week to week for Sam," Macdonald said; he won't go on IR. Lock is expected to start but was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough with a right elbow injury that has kept him out of the last two games. He went 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns at Arizona in Week 2. Jalen Milroe is getting added reps and Seattle signed Adrian Martinez to the practice squad. Shaheed did not practice Wednesday, per John Boyle via RotoWire, and needs some practice work to have a chance. Left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) also remains out, per NBC Sports.
events.so_what: Lock is a matchup streamer with an arm question, not a safe one, and a thrown-through elbow is what to watch on Friday's report. Jaxon Smith-Njigba stays a start, since his target volume doesn't depend on who is throwing. Keep Shaheed on the bench until he practices. Milroe has real konami upside if the elbow goes wrong, so he is a deep stash and nothing more until he is named.

events.headline: Jonah Coleman takes over the Denver backfield: career-high 41 snaps to J.K. Dobbins' season-low 13
events.detail: In the 28-24 win over Kansas City, Coleman had 11 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown plus four catches for 63 yards, with six red-zone and five goal-line carries. Dobbins had seven carries for 13 yards, no targets and no red-zone work, per RotoBaller. Sean Payton's backfield usage has shifted week to week before.
events.so_what: Goal-line work is the TD equity this scoring pays most for at running back, and Coleman now has all of it, which makes him a flex start with an RB2 ceiling. Dobbins drops to a bench hold until the split reverses.

brief.prose: A Browns second-round rookie (No. 39, out of Washington) who was camp's biggest surprise and has kept climbing: Monken promoted him to the first team, and Cleveland's unofficial depth chart now lists him as a starting outside 'X' opposite Jerry Jeudy, with fellow rookie KC Concepcion in the slot. The 6-4 target wins contested balls and is on track for a full-time Week 1 role. The cap is Cleveland's unsettled quarterback play (Watson/Sanders), but a rookie who has climbed to a starting job at a pick-156 price is a live half-PPR dart with real upside if the QB stabilizes.
brief.rationale: Rookie X-receiver who has ascended to a projected Week 1 starting role opposite Jeudy; deep-ADP half-PPR dart capped by Cleveland's shaky QB.

brief.prose: Stribling moved into extra first-team reps after Christian Kirk's camp calf strain, mastering the 'F'/slot spot, and analyst Adam Levitan floated that he may be 'flat better than Kirk' right now. But the room is crowded at the top: Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel headline it (Deebo at 'Z' in the injured Ricky Pearsall's spot), so Stribling is depth pushing for a rotational role, not a starter in waiting. Kubiak praised the flashes but said he still has 'a lot to learn' on route detail. A fragile opportunity that shrinks when Kirk is healthy; a deep watch, not a draftable role yet.
brief.rationale: Slot depth flashing with Kirk hurt, but buried behind Evans and Deebo; a fragile, injury-dependent opportunity rather than a real role.
